claim: J.P. Morgan Payments commercial inventory (P12 sub-products S01-S06) is complete
finding: Kinexys by J.P. Morgan / JPM Coin (ticker JPMD), a USD deposit token for institutional on-chain 24/7 payments, launched on Base on Nov 12, 2025. Not mentioned anywhere in the chapter (products or recent changes).
resolution: Add JPM-P12-S07 Kinexys / JPM Coin (JPMD) USD deposit token; recent change Nov 12, 2025: JPM Coin rolled out to institutional clients on Base.

claim: J.P. Morgan Payments disbursement options limited to the listed sub-products (incl. push-to-card)
finding: The J.P. Morgan Payments payables page lists "Emerging payments": real-time payments, Push to Card, Push to Wallet, Zelle, Interac and Prepaid Card. Push to Wallet, corporate Zelle disbursements and Interac (Canada) are not inventoried.
resolution: Add JPM-P12-S08 Emerging payments disbursements (Push to Wallet, Zelle, Interac, Prepaid Card), CONFIRMED_BANK S919.

claim: Push-to-card / real-time disbursements (Visa Direct / Mastercard Send); evidence CONFIRMED_BANK; sources []
finding: Sub-product carries CONFIRMED_BANK with an empty sources array. The bank page (S919) says "Push to Card" but does not name Visa Direct or Mastercard Send.
resolution: Name: "Push to Card (real-time card disbursements)"; sources ["S919"]; networks unconfirmed.

claim: SMB money-in is covered only by Zelle tags, QuickDeposit, ACH Collections
finding: Chase for Business markets an invoicing solution under "Collect & deposit" > "Create invoices" (mobile: "Pay & collect" > "Collect & deposit") where customers pay by card (same-day deposit at no extra cost), Zelle or check; QuickAccept card acceptance also sits in the same Collect & deposit hub. Not in the chapter.
resolution: Add invoicing as a sub-product (rail OTHER, with Zelle payment option); keep QuickAccept/POS out of scope but mention in notes.

claim: Receivables inventory (P12-S04) covers JPM inbound collection products
finding: J.P. Morgan Payments Pay-by-bank for billers (ACH rails + Mastercard open banking consent) went live Oct 20, 2023; not mentioned.
resolution: Add JPM-P12-S09 Pay-by-bank (ACH + Mastercard open banking), THIRD_PARTY; verify on jpmorgan.com in next pass.

claim: No in-app funding of PayPal/Venmo/Apple Cash is documented
finding: The Digital Services Agreement table of contents lists a "PayPal Provisioning Platform" addendum and a "Gifting Service" addendum (capture S910). These indicate a Chase-side PayPal card-provisioning flow and a gifting money-movement feature that the chapter does not inventory. Reviewer could not read the addendum bodies (PDF truncated in WebFetch; pdf.js blocked in the shared pane).
resolution: Keep P08 claims; add open questions: what the DSA "PayPal Provisioning Platform" and "Gifting Service" addenda enable and where they live in the UI. Settled by reading DSA pp. 85 and 97.

claim: No consumer instant external transfer (push-to-card / Visa Direct) and no consumer RTP/FedNow send
finding: Chase's Transfers Agreement (June 2026) and DSA Real-Time Payments addendum define consumer real-time sends with consumer limits; the chapter itself records this at JPM-P03-S04 and differentiator [5]. The weakness contradicts the data.
resolution: No consumer push-to-card; consumer RTP send is defined in the terms but not surfaced in any public UI/help content; external transfers remain 2-3 day ACH.

claim: Consumer Real-Time Payments Service is a sub-product of External transfers (product rails: ACH_EXTERNAL_TRANSFER only)
finding: The terms treat it as a separate "Real-Time Payments Service" with its own limits, irrevocability and send/RfP rules; JPM-P03 rails list omits RTP, so the rail rollup undercounts.
resolution: Keep nesting; add RTP to JPM-P03 rails; note "terms-level service, no consumer UI label found".

claim: Bill pay status labels, edit/cancel steps and limits are not published
finding: The Bill Payment Service addendum publishes statuses (Pending, Funded, Sent, Processed, Completed, Funds Needed, Funding Failed, Cancelled), cancel rules and a $100,000/day default maximum; the chapter's own P05 description and strength [6] say so.
resolution: Bill pay statuses, cancel rules and limits are published only in the DSA (not in help/marketing pages); autopay setup is buried under Payment Activity.

claim: States Pending, Funded, Sent, Completed, Cancelled (evidence INFERRED)
finding: DSA Bill Payment addendum lists the full vocabulary; evidence should be CONFIRMED_BANK and the list should include Processed, Funds Needed, Funding Failed.
resolution: states_shown: Pending, Funded, Sent, Processed, Completed, Funds Needed, Funding Failed, Cancelled (CONFIRMED_BANK, S910).

claim: External transfer states: Pending, In Process, Completed, Funding Failed, Cancelled
finding: The Transfers Agreement (June 2026) uses Pending, Funded, Sent, Completed, Funds Needed, Funding Failed, Cancelled; "In Process" does not appear (it is a Zelle term).
resolution: states_shown: Pending, Sent, Completed, Funds Needed, Funding Failed, Cancelled (CONFIRMED_BANK, S957/S910).

claim: Enrolled recipient receives funds typically within minutes; some up to 1-3 business days
finding: For sending, Chase states select transactions may take 1 to 2 business days; 1 to 3 business days applies to receiving from another bank.
resolution: Usually a few minutes; select transactions next business day (Chase recipient) or 1-2 business days (other bank).

claim: Pay-as-you-go RTP/FedNow send for small businesses at 1% capped $25
finding: Chase's own guides describe SMB real-time payments only as the TCH RTP network ("60% of accounts can receive"); FedNow appears only in a May 2024 press quote about Chase participation generally. Same issue in strengths[1], JPM-P09 rails (FEDNOW), JPM-P09-S03 name and JPM-J15 title.
resolution: SMB wording: "Pay-as-you-go real-time payments (TCH RTP per Chase guide; FedNow routing unconfirmed) at 1% capped $25"; P09 FEDNOW rail marked INFERRED. Open question retained.

claim: Schedule a cash withdrawal (in-app, pick up at ATM) — CONFIRMED_BANK
finding: Both the personal and business "Schedule a withdrawal" helpful-tips URLs now redirect to /digital/atms, which no longer mentions scheduled withdrawals (the sitemap still links them). The chapter itself records the page retirement in recent_changes[10] but keeps the capability as CONFIRMED_BANK, and JPM-J12/MANAGE/8 repeats it.
resolution: Evidence downgraded to INFERRED; open question added. Settled by an in-app check or a current Chase page describing scheduled ATM withdrawals.

claim: Consumer wire states Pending, In Process, Completed, Cancelled — CONFIRMED_BANK
finding: Wire FAQs and the wire addendum describe the Wire activity page and Action column but list no consumer status labels; the only published wire labels are Connect's (Scheduled, Processing, Sent, Failed, Needs approval).
resolution: Consumer wire status labels: INFERRED (no published list); Connect labels shown as the nearest bank-documented vocabulary.

claim: SMB wire states Pending approval, Pending, In process, Completed (INFERRED)
finding: Connect Wires Go-To Guide (Oct 2026) — same Chase business UI family — publishes Scheduled, Processing, Sent, Failed, Needs approval.
resolution: states_shown: Scheduled, Processing, Sent, Failed, Needs approval (Connect-confirmed; INFERRED for Chase Business Online).

claim: Chase Connect wires — evidence INFERRED
finding: The Connect Domestic and International Wires Go-To Guide (Oct 2026) documents the path, statuses, approvals and "Report a problem" recall.
resolution: JPM-P11-S02 evidence CONFIRMED_BANK, sources S926, S063.

claim: Consumer wire send flow has no published step-by-step guide and no public scam-interstitial wording
finding: Step guide claim holds (helpful-tips page retired). But public scam wording exists: DSA wire addendum "Protect Yourself Against Wire Scams" red-flag list and Security Center wire guidance — the chapter cites this itself in differentiator [6].
resolution: No public step-by-step consumer wire guide; in-flow interstitial text not public; wire-scam red flags published in DSA wire addendum and Security Center.

claim: Recent changes list is complete
finding: Sept 16, 2025: JPMorganChase and Plaid announced a renewed data-access agreement with a pricing structure (Chase charging aggregators) — relevant to instant external-account verification and third-party P2P funding.
resolution: Add: "Sep 16, 2025 — JPMorganChase–Plaid renewed data-access agreement introduces a pricing structure for aggregator access (bank press release)."

claim: Recent changes list is complete (Zelle legal context)
finding: Aug 13, 2025: New York Attorney General sued Early Warning Services (Zelle operator, co-owned by JPMorgan Chase) over fraud controls, after the CFPB dropped its case.
resolution: Add: "Aug 2025 — NY AG sued Early Warning Services (Zelle operator; Chase is a co-owner) over scam/fraud controls (network-level, THIRD_PARTY)."

claim: zelle = true (THIRD_PARTY)
finding: Chase's own Zelle page and Zelle Service Terms confirm participation.
resolution: zelle: true, CONFIRMED_BANK (S001, S042).

claim: rtp_receive = true (THIRD_PARTY)
finding: Transfers Agreement / DSA RTP addendum ("send payments to and receive payments from ... Real-Time Payments System") and J.P. Morgan RTP/FedNow page ("Receive and pay funds within seconds") are bank sources.
resolution: rtp_receive: true, CONFIRMED_BANK (S910, S915, S050).

claim: push_to_card = true (CONFIRMED_BANK, S919)
finding: True only for J.P. Morgan Payments corporate disbursements; no consumer or SMB push-to-card exists (chapter open question 0). The third-party rails matrix records "unknown".
resolution: push_to_card: true (commercial disbursements via J.P. Morgan Payments only; no consumer/SMB push-to-card).

claim: fednow_send = true (CONFIRMED_BANK) — third-party matrix says unknown
finding: Reviewer could not parse the FRB participant XLSX (proxy and page CSP blocked) to check send vs receive split; the the participation baseline matrix records fednow_send "unknown".
resolution: fednow_send: true (J.P. Morgan Payments commercial; not documented for Chase consumer/SMB channels). the participation baseline "unknown" should be updated from S915.

claim: International wire – USD capabilities: recurring = true, scheduled_future_dated = true
finding: DSA wire addendum allows repeating/future-dated transfers "except for Consumer International Funds Transfers"; for consumers, USD international wires are Consumer International Funds Transfers (30-minute cancel window applies). The chapter's own J08 MANAGE step says so.
resolution: Keep flags true for business; add other_flags {"consumer_recurring_or_future_dated": false} and note.

claim: International wire – foreign currency (FX wire / global transfer)
finding: The bank's terms name the service "Chase Global Transfer" (Online Wire Transfer and Chase Global Transfer Services addendum); sign-in entry is "sign-in-global-transfers".
resolution: Name: "Chase Global Transfer (international wire in foreign currency)".

claim: Most transparent SMB payables rail in the peer set
finding: Peer-comparative superlative cannot be verified from this chapter's sources alone.
resolution: Original stands as analyst judgement; FedNow portion corrected under JPM-C013. Synthesis team should confirm the peer superlative.

claim: Recipient has 9 succeeding business days to enroll, else cancelled (~10 days)
finding: Zelle Service Terms are internally inconsistent: section 11(d) says nine succeeding Business Days but later refers to a "ten (10) day period".
resolution: Original wording stands; it already reflects both numbers in the terms.

claim: Funds land in business checking usually within minutes; no incoming limit
finding: Business Zelle FAQ describes only a daily send limit; it does not state that incoming payments are unlimited.
resolution: "Usually within minutes; no incoming (receive) limit is published."
